## What it is

An open-topped tray with four full-height walls, rounded at the corners, and a
window cut into the front wall so a stack of bags can be reached and pulled out
sideways instead of lifted from above. The side walls run full height all the way
to the front corners; only the front wall is notched, and only across its middle.
The cavity floor ramps up near the front to meet the bottom of that opening flush,
so there's no lip for an item to catch on while it's being slid out.

## Design notes

Proportions are taste, not fit, and are plain sliders: `length`, `width`, `height`,
`front_height`, `gap_fraction`, `corner_radius`. Nothing here mates with a
manufactured part, so none of it is measured.

`gap_fraction` sets the opening's width as a fraction of the box's own width
(0.8 by default, i.e. 80%), centered on the front wall, leaving a solid pillar of
wall on each side that blends into the rounded front corners. The cut only punches
through the front wall's own thickness; the side walls are never touched.

`ramp_length` sets how far back from the front the floor's slope reaches before
levelling out to the ordinary flat floor. The rise is not a separate slider: it's
always exactly `front_height`, so the ramp's peak lands flush with the opening's
lower edge with no step. A shorter `ramp_length` makes a steeper ramp; a longer one
a gentler, more gradual one.

`ramp_radius` bows the ramp into a shallow curve instead of a flat slope, using a
true circular arc between the same two endpoints the straight ramp used (so
`ramp_length` and `front_height` still mean exactly what they say). Set it to 0 for
the original flat ramp.

## Don't

- Don't extend the front cut into the side walls. An earlier version lowered the
  side walls near the front too (a wraparound scoop), which also put sliver chamfer
  faces at the step-meets-corner points. Keeping the side walls full height and
  cutting only a window in the front is the simpler shape, but it has the same class
  of sliver at the top corners of the window, so there's still a count to accept.
- Don't try to chamfer away the 4 sliver faces where the window's top corners meet
  the pillar edges. They're the doctrine's sanctioned case: three 1mm polish
  chamfers converging at a convex corner, ~0.87mm2 each. Whether they show up
  depends on the exact dimensions (present at this part's current size, absent at
  some others tried while flexing the sliders) — accept the count on the card
  rather than chasing it per-size.
- Don't drop `gap_fraction` close to 1 without also shrinking `corner_radius`: the
  part refuses to build if the wall left beside the opening is too thin once the
  corner rounding eats into it.
- The ramp's extra material in the front sill is also what keeps that area above
  the printer's minimum wall thickness — a thin spot used to show up right there
  before the ramp existed. Don't thin the ramp down without rechecking that.
- Don't drop `ramp_radius` below the floor this part's math works out for the
  current `ramp_length`/`front_height` (the refusal message names the number).
  This ramp is shallow — a long, low rise — so a circular arc between its two
  fixed ends only stays above the floor past a fairly large radius; a smaller one
  swings the curve down through the floor and splits the ramp into a detached
  sliver instead of one solid. That's also why the visible bow is gentle rather
  than dramatic: it's the most curve this shape can take without breaking.
- Don't try rounding the ramp by filleting the corner where it lifts off the
  floor instead. It looked promising (bounded, can't swing out of range) but the
  corner there is acute enough that any useful radius eats nearly the whole ramp
  length and reads to the overhang checker as a long, nearly-flat unsupported
  shelf, even though it's sitting right on the floor underneath. The chord-preserving
  arc above doesn't have that problem.

## Changelog

- 2026-10-03: built as an open-topped scoop-front tray, styled after a photo of a
  wooden note holder.
- 2026-10-03: side walls now run full height to the front; the opening is a
  centered window in the front wall only, sized at 80% of the box's width.
  Added a refusal for a gap_fraction/corner_radius combination that leaves the
  wall beside the opening too thin.
- 2026-10-03: added a Gridfinity-compatible base, sized to the smallest grid that
  holds the tray's footprint. Grid pitch and foot profile recorded in
  `measurements.toml` against the published spec. Foot corners are mitred rather
  than rounded to avoid a checker false-positive on curved 45 degree surfaces.
- 2026-10-03: added a ramp to the cavity floor near the front, rising to meet the
  opening flush so items slide out instead of catching on the sill's inside edge.
  Fixed the earlier front-sill min_wall thinness as a side effect; accepted the
  Gridfinity foot's own, unrelated min_wall reading at 0.7, same as the doctrine's
  own gridfinity precedent.
- 2026-10-03: removed the Gridfinity base. The tray sits flat on the bed again;
  the ramp and its min_wall fix stay. `measurements.toml`'s gridfinity_* entries
  are unused now but left on file in case the base comes back.
- 2026-10-03: added `ramp_radius` to bow the ramp into a curve instead of a flat
  slope, as a circular arc between the ramp's existing two endpoints. Refuses a
  radius too tight for the current ramp_length/front_height to stay clear of the
  floor.
